Assignment **HCAL-20261015-CaloTech** completed read-only at input revision **`5b4e5d9e563505aea17e9b792458708c3175ec4a`**. No files changed, dependency setup, simulation, or further delegation.

**Conclusion — INFERENCE:** steel/scintillator remains a credible HCAL technology for a hadron collider, especially centrally. The present evidence does **not** qualify a warm, uniformly instrumented CALICE-like SiPM-on-tile calorimeter across the whole barrel/endcap. The major unresolved choice is the complete operating/readout/radiation architecture. Retain the human’s technology preference while keeping the most exposed endcap regions conditional on radiation evidence.

The current nODD prototypes improve physical accounting substantially. Their successful geometry checks establish internally consistent prototype geometry, not collider operation or engineering feasibility.

### Verified public evidence and catalogue-ready metadata

All sources accessed **2026-10-15**. No new local reference copies or hashes were created.

1. **Existing `SRC-CALICE-AHCAL-2022`:** CALICE Collaboration, *Design, Construction and Commissioning of a Technological Prototype of a Highly Granular SiPM-on-tile Scintillator-Steel Hadronic Calorimeter*, **arXiv:2209.15327v1, 2022-09-30**. Actual primary HTML inspected:  
   [Versioned paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2209.15327v1).

   **FACT:** §§2.1–2.2 describe 360 × 360 mm HBUs, 144 directly coupled SiPM/tile channels, 3 mm scintillator and 30 mm tile pitch; §2.7 describes 6.4 mm cassettes including two 0.5 mm steel covers. §§2.3–2.3.1 explicitly describe acquisition followed by digitization/readout, 16-cell analog memory, BUSY stopping acquisition, selectable 250 kHz–5 MHz bunch clock, and ILC power pulsing. The distributed 40 MHz clock is divided down by the DIF (§2.3.2). §2.8 cools interface boards; active-layer cooling is omitted because of pulsed low consumption. This is tested technological-prototype evidence, principally for electron–positron collider conditions.

2. **Suggested `SRC-ATLAS-TILE-RUN2-2025`:** ATLAS Collaboration, *Operation and performance of the ATLAS tile calorimeter in LHC Run 2*, **arXiv:2401.16034v2, 2025-01-10**; CERN-EP-2023-266; *Eur. Phys. J. C* **84 (2024) 1313**; DOI **10.1140/epjc/s10052-024-13151-4**.  
   [Versioned primary HTML](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.16034v2).

   **FACT:** §§2.1–2.2 describe operating low-carbon-steel/plastic-scintillator calorimetry, fibre/PMT readout and continuous digitization every 25 ns with triggered pipeline extraction. Its barrel technology covers approximately |η| < 1.7; forward/endcap calorimetry uses different active technology. §§5.1–5.2 report measured radiation-related optical degradation and dose-rate/annealing uncertainties. The abstract reports 99.65% data-taking efficiency during 2015–2018. This demonstrates the absorber/active-medium combination at a hadron collider; it does not demonstrate nODD’s embedded one-SiPM-per-tile implementation.

3. **Suggested `SRC-CMS-RUN3-2024`:** CMS Collaboration, *Development of the CMS detector for the CERN LHC Run 3*, **arXiv:2309.05466v2, 2024-05-30**; CMS-PRF-21-001, CERN-EP-2023-136; *JINST* **19 (2024) P05064**; DOI **10.1088/1748-0221/19/05/P05064**.  
   [Versioned primary HTML](https://arxiv.org/html/2309.05466v2).

   **FACT:** §5.2, “Frontend readout card,” describes QIE11 integrating in 25 ns buckets, ADC/TDC data, radiation-tolerant conversion and optical links. “Photodetector control” describes individual SiPM bias regulation, current measurement/protection, Peltier control and temperature/humidity monitoring. “Optical decoder unit” shows fibre transport and aggregation before SiPM readout; this is a different packaging architecture from on-tile electronics. §5.5 and Figure 35 show irradiation-related dark-current evolution. The inspected HTML displays section numbers as **0.5.2/0.5.5**; use the named subsections as unambiguous locators. Version metadata is authoritative; the HTML’s automatically rendered title-page date is inconsistent with it.

4. **Suggested `SRC-HGCROC-PRODUCTION-2026`:** F. Bouyjou et al., *Design to production of HGCROC3 and H2GCROC3: radiation-hard front-end ASICs for the CMS HGCAL*, published **2026-01-19**, *JINST* **21 (2026) C01016**; DOI **10.1088/1748-0221/21/01/C01016**. Complete seven-page publication PDF inspected; CC BY 4.0 stated.  
   [Actual publication PDF]([external URL redacted; see source journal]).

   **FACT:** §1, printed p.1/PDF2, distinguishes H2GCROC3 for SiPM tiles from HGCROC3 for silicon; describes bunch-crossing trigger sums, 512-depth latency memory, 32-depth output FIFO, and a **design requirement below 15 mW/channel**. §§2–3, printed pp.2–5/PDF3–6, document real revision-dependent mixed-signal/SEE failures and mitigation. The source describes radiation-selected scintillator regions and chips in production, with lab/beam/irradiation evidence. It does not establish that a generic 36-channel package or 5 mW/channel assumption is equivalent.

5. **Suggested `SRC-CMS-SIPM-UPGRADE-2026`:** A. Heering, A. Karneyeu, Y. Musienko and M. Wayne, *Silicon Photomultipliers in the CMS Upgrade*, **arXiv:2606.13956v1, 2026-06-11**, proceedings submitted to JINST.  
   [Version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13956v1), [primary PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.13956).

   **FACT:** §3.1, printed pp.4–6/PDF4–6, reports HGCAL SiPM requirements through **5 × 10¹³ n_eq/cm²**, cold irradiation measurements, sensor selection, packaging and production/QC. Quoted sensor performance conditions include **−35 °C**, and Figure 4 measurements were at approximately **−36 °C**. These are component/test-condition facts, not a universal SiPM fluence limit. The text contains an apparently reversed η description of silicon/scintillator placement; do **not** import that statement. Use the production ASIC paper’s lower-radiation-region description.

6. **Suggested `SRC-CMS-HGCAL-COLDTEST-2026`:** CMS Communications, *HGCAL keeps its cool in major testing milestone*, **2026-07-24**.  
   [Official construction report]([external URL redacted; see source journal]).

   **FACT:** paragraphs beginning “A giant, highly controlled freezer,” “To tackle…” and “To prevent…” report cold testing of the **first** large absorber structure: −35 °C interior, regulated exterior thermal screens, monitoring and dry-air flushing. The 170-tonne steel structure was cooled using test aluminium plates. This is demonstrated structural/environmental testing; the article explicitly places active-cassette insertion later. Do not describe it as completed operation of the whole HGCAL.

### Exact nODD gaps

The following are **FACT about the pinned model**, followed by their **INFERENCE** implications. Locators are relative to the assigned revision.

| Area | Existing representation | Remaining realism gap |
|---|---|---|
| Sampling/BOM | DES027 retains ODD’s 36 × (30 mm steel + 16 mm `siPCBMix` + 3 mm scintillator + 2 mm air); DES028 substitutes explicit parts | This substitution changes shower material and containment. It needs an attributable old/new constituent and interaction-length comparison, not treatment as a neutral geometry refactor. |
| Tile package | `cassettes.json:hcal` and `model.py:build_hcal`: 29.7 mm tile, 30 mm pitch, 0.1 mm PET shell, cylindrical recess, effective SiPM package and per-tile LED | Useful bulk geometry, but the shell/recess/package are project choices. Reflector optical properties, real dimple profile, coupling/air gap, adhesive, PCB support and mounting cut-outs need sourced effective-model contracts. |
| Scintillator material | `model.py:materials` retains ODD `Polystyrene` C19H21 at 1.032 g/cm³ | This is a comparison proxy, not a specified manufactured scintillator. Review real polymer/fluor chemistry, especially hydrogen content for hadronic response; retain old material as control. |
| Front end | Four 36-channel 10 × 10 × 1.2 mm effective packages; 5 mW/channel and 2 W/interface assumptions | No selected component establishes footprint, continuous throughput, trigger buffering, dynamic range, radiation tolerance or dissipation. A continuous readout architecture is a design gate. Adding cooling alone does not resolve acquisition dead time. |
| Thermal system | 1 mm Cu spreader, graphite pads/posts, 2 mm OD/1.6 mm ID Ti/water tubes; 20 °C, ΔT = 5 K | These provide material and ideal heat-balance accounting. They do not establish thermal resistance, heat spreading, SiPM temperature stability, pressure drop, manifolding, leak control or irradiated dark-current heat. |
| Services | Face ports and local tubes; DES029 edge/end reservations | No connected network, real connectors, voltage-drop analysis, data aggregation, bias regulation/current protection or external HCAL service ledger. Reservations do not supply these components. |
| Segmentation/coverage | One cell per physical tile; 400 × 380 mm cassettes | The channel definition is substantially improved, but fixed large rectangles create major unsensed absorber regions. Logical granularity does not compensate for missing modules. |
| Mechanics/material | Separate sector absorbers, rails, skins and frames | Absorber joining, support load paths, flatness/insertion allowance, magnetic grade/B–H and forces, access and replaceability remain open. Nonmagnetic CALICE steel precedent cannot qualify `Steel235`. |

Two useful independent calculations from the pinned input, **INFERENCE**:

- The **1 mm Cu spreader plus two 0.5 mm stainless skins contribute 2.5104 kg**, approximately **75.6%** of the 3.318896 kg cassette mass. Their dimensions therefore deserve physical justification before blanket replication.
- At the unchanged heat formula, a **proposed sensitivity point** of 15 rather than 5 mW/channel increases ideal cassette heat **3.0381 → 4.6381 W** and ideal flow **0.1454 → 0.2219 g/s**. This is not a prediction for an H2GCROC implementation: channel overhead, interfaces, conversion and radiation current would also change.

DES029’s model has **36,416 HCAL cassettes/5,243,904 channels**. The assumed interface allowance alone is **72.832 kW before conversion loss**. Shared interfaces deserve study, provided the relocated circuitry, material, links and heat remain accounted for.

### Bounded next path

All entries below are **proposed NODD DESIGN CHOICES, unsigned**.

1. **Operating and regional suitability contract.** Establish bunch spacing, occupancy/rate scenarios, trigger latency/readout strategy, lifetime fluence/TID/dose-rate maps, temperature range and access assumptions. Until supplied, retain a conditional central steel/scintillator design and evaluate endcap regions separately. Do not invent a luminosity or claim HL-LHC qualification.

2. **One actual tile/SiPM channel.** Choose a publicly documented scintillator, reflector, SiPM package and optical coupling. Record geometry, materials, cold/warm and irradiated characteristics, MIP detection margin, saturation/recovery and calibration accessibility. Preserve the current 30 mm/3 mm option as the comparison, not automatic final optimization.

3. **One continuous-readout board.** Compare a direct on-tile architecture with an explicit H2GCROC-class implementation contract and a fibre-export alternative where useful. Specify full channel/buffer/link/power/control/BOM ownership. Component provenance must precede freezing cassette dimensions.

4. **One cooled cassette plus realistic service handoff.** Rework the heat path and connector/manifold zone from the selected board, including an adverse irradiated-current case. Validate mass/material/IDs/containment and engineering plausibility separately. Specify what thermal or hydraulic calculations remain conditional.

5. **An inner endcap carrier and a barrel strip, then complete layers.** Follow the ECAL method of separating mechanical carriers from readout boards and sharing interfaces. Use small standard tile-board families, e.g. proposed 6 × 6/6 × 12 arrays, and explicitly engineered boundary units. Do not computationally clip standard tiles. Repair the large inner/aperture holes before relying on staggering.

6. **Coupled ECAL–HCAL layer/sector gates.** Publish active masks and active-layer crossings versus η/φ, including interfaces, seams and routes. Recalculate counts, heat, mass, material and cable/coolant capacity. Validate combined ECAL + HCAL transport, leakage and timing windows before assigning calorimeter performance. SysArch owns global service/steel interfaces; CaloTech retains coupled ECAL/HCAL integration ownership; SoftEng implements response; PhysVal evaluates its scientific meaning.

Actual checks: pinned `git show` inspection of the assigned five files plus `cassettes.json`, `model.py`, DES029 repair proposal, DES034 and its source register; branch/HEAD/status inspection; public primary-text/PDF examination; read-only Python arithmetic above. **No native or response validation was rerun.** DES030/031 are referenced external proposal revisions rather than files at the assigned commit; I have not treated their implementation as independently inspected evidence.
